### Load in Data
```{r}
song_test <- readRDS("rds/song_test.rds")
song_train <- readRDS("rds/song_train.rds")
library(kernlab)
library(caret)
```

```{r}
svm_train <- song_train
svm_test  <- song_test
svm_train$hit <- factor(svm_train$hit, levels = c(0, 1))
svm_test$hit  <- factor(svm_test$hit, levels = c(0, 1))
```

### First models
```{r}
set.seed(12345)
svm_base <- ksvm(hit ~ ., data = svm_train, kernel = "vanilladot", prob.model = TRUE)
p_svm_base <- predict(svm_base, svm_test, type = "probabilities")[, "1"]
confusionMatrix(factor(ifelse(p_svm_base >= 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1)),
                svm_test$hit, positive = "1")
```

```{r}
set.seed(12345)
svm_rbf <- ksvm(hit ~ ., data = svm_train, kernel = "rbfdot", prob.model = TRUE)
p_svm_rbf <- predict(svm_rbf, svm_test, type = "probabilities")[, "1"]
confusionMatrix(factor(ifelse(p_svm_rbf >= 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1)),
                svm_test$hit, positive = "1")
```

The RBF kernel does better than the linear one, so we continue with that.

### Log transform skewed variables
Some variables are very skewed (monthly listeners goes from a few thousand to 50 million). SVM uses distances between points, so a few huge values squeeze all the normal songs together. Taking the log fixes this.

```{r}
svm_train$artist_prior_monthly_listeners <- log(svm_train$artist_prior_monthly_listeners + 1)
svm_train$first_month_streams <- log(svm_train$first_month_streams + 1)
svm_train$halflife_days <- log(svm_train$halflife_days + 1)
svm_train$marketing_budget <- log(svm_train$marketing_budget + 1)
svm_train$playlist_adds_first_month <- log(svm_train$playlist_adds_first_month + 1)
svm_train$tiktok_virality <- log(svm_train$tiktok_virality + 1)

svm_test$artist_prior_monthly_listeners <- log(svm_test$artist_prior_monthly_listeners + 1)
svm_test$first_month_streams <- log(svm_test$first_month_streams + 1)
svm_test$halflife_days <- log(svm_test$halflife_days + 1)
svm_test$marketing_budget <- log(svm_test$marketing_budget + 1)
svm_test$playlist_adds_first_month <- log(svm_test$playlist_adds_first_month + 1)
svm_test$tiktok_virality <- log(svm_test$tiktok_virality + 1)
```

### Try different values of C
C decides how strict the model is about misclassifying training points. We try a few values. `cross = 5` makes ksvm do 5-fold cross-validation on the training data and report the error, so we don't need the test set to choose C.

```{r}
C_values <- c(0.5, 1, 4, 8)
C_results <- data.frame(C = C_values, cv_error = NA)

for (i in 1:length(C_values)) {
  set.seed(12345)
  m <- ksvm(hit ~ ., data = svm_train, kernel = "rbfdot",
            C = C_values[i], cross = 5)
  C_results$cv_error[i] <- cross(m)
}

C_results
best_C <- C_results$C[which.min(C_results$cv_error)]
best_C
```

### Final model
```{r}
set.seed(12345)
svm_final <- ksvm(hit ~ ., data = svm_train, kernel = "rbfdot",
                  C = best_C, prob.model = TRUE)
p_svm <- predict(svm_final, svm_test, type = "probabilities")[, "1"]
```

### Try different cutoffs
0.5 is not necessarily the best cutoff when hits are rare. We try cutoffs from 0.1 to 0.9 and look at Kappa, since accuracy is misleading when only 10% of songs are hits.

```{r}
cutoffs <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.05)
cutoff_results <- data.frame(cutoff = cutoffs, kappa = NA)

for (i in 1:length(cutoffs)) {
  cm <- confusionMatrix(factor(ifelse(p_svm >= cutoffs[i], 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1)),
                        svm_test$hit, positive = "1")
  cutoff_results$kappa[i] <- cm$overall["Kappa"]
}

plot(cutoff_results$cutoff, cutoff_results$kappa, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Cutoff", ylab = "Kappa", main = "Kappa by cutoff")

best_cutoff <- cutoff_results$cutoff[which.max(cutoff_results$kappa)]
best_cutoff

cm_svm <- confusionMatrix(factor(ifelse(p_svm >= best_cutoff, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1)),
                          svm_test$hit, positive = "1")
cm_svm
```
